claims.appliesTo: Every profile whose estate fact cites the $15M US exemption (2026): 96 profile files, non-US and US alike
claims.claim: The US estate tax basic exclusion amount for deaths in 2026 is $15,000,000 (the profiles' "$15M US exemption (2026)")

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
sources.says: "Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000", up from $13,990,000 for 2025; the release (October 9, 2025) cites Revenue Procedure 2025-32 and is marked as an archival document.

claims.note: No change needed in any profile. The amount is per decedent (each estate). Wording variants, all covered: "the $15M US exemption (2026) applies as anywhere"; "US estate tax applies above the $15M exemption (2026)"; "so only US estate tax applies, above the $15M exemption (2026)"; "US estate tax applies only above the $15M exemption (2026)"; "heirs also face the federal estate tax above the $15M exemption (2026)" and "heirs owe only the federal estate tax above the $15M exemption (2026)" (US profiles); "the $15M US exemption (2026) is the only relief" (Dubai); "below the $15M US exemption (2026)" (Canada, South Africa); "the federal $15M exemption (2026)" (Minnesota). The IRS page calls the law the Working Families Tax Cuts and the news release calls it the One, Big, Beautiful Bill; both name Public Law 119-21.

claims.appliesTo: Context for the same estate facts: no profile states it, but each dates the figure "(2026)"
claims.claim: $15,000,000 is the amount written into the statute, and it is indexed for inflation for deaths after 2026

sources.name: Cornell Legal Information Institute: 26 U.S. Code § 2010, unified credit against estate tax
sources.says: Subsection (c)(3)(A): "the basic exclusion amount is $15,000,000". (c)(3)(B): for a decedent dying in a calendar year after 2026 the amount is increased by the cost-of-living adjustment under section 1(f)(3), with calendar year 2025 as the base year, rounded to the nearest multiple of $10,000. The notes credit the change to Pub. L. 119-21, for estates of decedents dying after December 31, 2025.

claims.note: The three IRS pages read for us-estate-exemption-2026 give the 2026 amount but do not say whether it is indexed; the statute text was read on Cornell's copy of the US Code, not on a government site. Keep the "(2026)" date in the profiles: the figure rises from 2027. A search result (not a page read) reported a 2027 amount set by a Rev. Proc. 2026-35; that is unverified and is not used here.

sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. claims.rankFlag: For EU residents this removes the one reported way to draw cash against the portfolio, which is the borrow step of buy-borrow-die. It touches every EU pick, the top two included (Algarve 1, Lisbon 2), and the lending rubric in src/data/expatPicks.ts, whose score 3 reads "IBKR only, or EU residence where Schwab reportedly restricts cash-out by margin": if IBKR restricts it too, EU profiles may belong at 2 ("IBKR only, and even that uncertain") or the rubric needs a line of its own. Neither the scores nor the rubric were changed here: user's call.
claims.rankResolved: The rubric's lending 2 already reads "or EU residence, where Schwab and IBKR's EU entity both reportedly bar taking cash out through margin" (the EU scores moved to 2 in the fact check), and every ranked pick that scores lending 2 now says "borrowing cash against the portfolio is reportedly blocked for residents" in its `why`; ranks unchanged.
claims.note: Why corrected and not cant-confirm: the profiles tell the reader to plan on IBKR margin for cash, and every page read on the point says the opposite for accounts carried by IBKR's Irish entity. Why the new wording still says "reportedly": IBKR's own statement could not be read. Its knowledge-base articles 3750 ("TWS Account Window for Retail Clients of IBKR Ireland and Central Europe", https://ibkb.interactivebrokers.com/article/3750) and 4581 returned HTTP 403; a search result, which is not a read, quotes 3750 as saying a retail client is "not permitted to withdraw from the margin facility" when already borrowing or when the withdrawal would create a loan. A later builder should try that article again, and if it reads as quoted, drop "reportedly". Nothing read says whether a client reclassified as professional may withdraw. Apply the standard wording to the EU profiles only. London's variant, "which likely covers the UK, so plan on IBKR margin", is about IB UK, where the only evidence is the forum anecdote above: the UK builder treats it as a cant-confirm of its own. Swiss residents are reported to be with IB UK and able to withdraw; that is anecdote too. In place, the standard wording reads: "..., but Schwab reportedly bars Europe residents from taking cash out through margin, and IBKR's EU entity reportedly lends on margin only to buy securities, not to withdraw as cash, so confirm how you would draw cash before relying on either; EU PRIIPs rules ...". Added by the Portugal builder on 2026-11-15: the search snippet quoting "not permitted to withdraw from the margin facility" appears to come from IBKR Australia's help article, not article 3750, so it is no evidence for IBKR Ireland; the correction rests on the LYNX and CapTrader help pages and the IBIE customer agreement. Article 3750 and IBKR's country list returned HTTP 403 again on a second try the same day. The plan's decision of 2026-11-15 settled what the rankFlag left open: EU profiles' lending score goes 3 → 2 as each country is checked, and the rubric's lines for 3 and 2 were reworded in src/data/expatPicks.ts and src/data/profiles/README.md (2 = IBKR only and even that uncertain, or EU residence, where Schwab and IBKR's EU entity both reportedly bar taking cash out through margin). Portugal's six profiles carry the standard wording unchanged, the drawback "Schwab and IBKR both reportedly bar drawing margin as cash", and a closing summary sentence: "The weak point is the borrow step: Schwab and IBKR both reportedly bar EU residents from drawing margin as cash."

claims.appliesTo: The rule behind every EU profile's PRIIPs clause (34 profile files mention PRIIPs)
claims.claim: Under the EU PRIIPs Regulation a packaged retail product may be made available or sold to a retail investor only with a key information document (KID)

sources.name: Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014, Article 5, as adopted (legislation.gov.uk copy of the EU text)
sources.says: Article 5(1): "Before a PRIIP is made available to retail investors, the PRIIP manufacturer shall draw up" a key information document for that product in accordance with the Regulation, and publish it on its website. The page shows the original version as adopted by the EU.

sources.name: Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014, Article 13, as adopted (legislation.gov.uk copy of the EU text)
sources.says: Article 13(1): "A person advising on, or selling, a PRIIP shall provide retail investors with the key information document" in good time before those retail investors are bound by any contract or offer relating to that PRIIP. The article puts duties on those who advise or sell; it says nothing about an investor selling or keeping a PRIIP already held.

sources.name: European Commission: Key information documents for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs)
sources.says: The PRIIPs Regulation (1286/2014/EU) "obliges those who produce or sell investment products to provide investors with key information documents (KIDs)" of no more than three pages. The page does not mention non-EU funds or what happens to a product with no KID.

claims.note: The Regulation was read in the originally adopted text on the UK government's legislation site, because EUR-Lex returned an empty page to WebFetch (three URL forms tried). That copy does not show later EU amendments; the two articles quoted are the core duty. The Regulation never names US ETFs: the block is how brokers apply it to funds whose managers publish no KID (see priips-us-etf-new-buys-blocked).

claims.appliesTo: EU profiles' lending facts: "EU PRIIPs rules reportedly block new buys of US-listed ETFs" (24 profiles) and "EU PRIIPs rules reportedly block new purchases of US ETFs" (Athens, Crete, Paphos, Limassol, Sliema)

claims.note: Confirmed on a broker's own help page and a dated secondary page, with the rule itself in priips-kid-required. The profiles' "reportedly" may stay; it is not wrong. IBKR's own knowledge-base articles on PRIIPs (https://ibkb.interactivebrokers.com/node/3324 and /node/2993) returned HTTP 403. Not settled here: who counts as an EU retail client for a resident of a non-EU country. Antalya, Istanbul and Kotor say "as a non-EU country, PRIIPs limits on US ETFs do not apply" without a hedge, and Sarandë says the limit "should not apply"; that depends on which IBKR entity carries the account, which no page read here states. sources.name: Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014, Article 13, as adopted (legislation.gov.uk copy of the EU text)

sources.says: Article 4(6): "retail investor" means "a retail client as defined in point (11) of Article 4(1) of Directive 2014/65/EU", or an insurance customer who would not qualify as a professional client under that Directive.

sources.name: Interactive Brokers Ireland Limited: Customer Agreement (document 4750, 7/1/2023), copy hosted by LYNX
sources.says: Appendix 1, point 3: "The requirements to deliver certain product-specific documents, such as Key Investor Information Documents (\"KIID\") for Packaged Retail and Insurance-based Investment Products (\"PRIIPs\"), are not applied to Professional Clients." sources.name: Banker on Wheels: Interactive Brokers review
sources.says: Last updated 2 November 2026. Access to US ETFs is limited to "elective professional clients", who must meet two of three tests: a year of relevant professional experience, a portfolio over €500k, or frequent large trades (an average of 10 a quarter over the previous four quarters).

claims.note: Useful to a retiree with a large portfolio, since the €500k test is one of the two needed; the second test is the hard one for a buy-and-hold investor. The three tests are from the secondary page, not from IBKR or the Directive, so a profile that mentions this route should say "reportedly". No profile needs to change.
